original_test_intent: Measure the LTSSM/PCIe operating margin of each approved motherboard slot and link with the platform-specific Intel SSV lab flow, then compare raw margin results and link behavior with the governing guide.
original_method: A qualified operator binds the physical slot/device/link, configures calibrated Intel SSV equipment exactly per the approved manual revision, performs each documented margin step under link/error observation, captures raw tool and probe data and restores the baseline configuration.
manual_activity: A qualified PCIe validation operator installs and controls probes/fixtures, executes margin points and any link-setting changes, observes physical/tool state and restores hardware. Automation may collect independent topology and event evidence only.
required_inputs: Exact SUT/board revision, PCIe slot, device, BDF, root/downstream port, generation and width matrix
Applicable Intel Server System Validation Manual revision and platform applicability
Intel SSV margin/debug tool versions and supported procedure
Probe/fixture/instrument identities, calibration certificates and connection diagram
Sweep axes, step sizes, dwell, safe boundaries and pass limits per link
Baseline/restore steps, dedicated lab window, console/OOB recovery and evidence format
safety_requirements: Do not guess margin voltages/timing, link parameters, slot targets or probe points
Preserve PCIe topology, settings and error baseline before any change
Use only calibrated approved fixtures and ESD/lab controls
Apply one documented margin step at a time with link, AER/DPC, device and thermal/power monitoring
Stop on link loss, unexpected retrain/downgrade, device disappearance, persistent PCIe error, probe fault or manual safety limit
Do not retry with improvised values or broaden the target
Remove fixtures and restore/verify all settings before release
agent_execution_scope: Validate the supplied identities, guide revision, calibration and expected matrix
Timestamp and organize operator/tool/probe outputs for every margin point
Correlate link transitions and AER/DPC/device events without controlling physical equipment
Compare raw values to the provided guide and verify restored read-only state
Do not select margins, attach probes, alter links or issue the final verdict
engineer_actions: Approve the governing guide, target matrix, sweep limits and recovery
Install/operate calibrated probes and Intel margin tools
Control all link-affecting settings and stop decisions
Restore hardware/configuration and own PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its direction to follow Intel SSV with probes is aligned, but there is no executable source command and no safe way to derive tool arguments or limits without the exact guide and platform setup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the command sequence printed in the approved Intel SSV manual for the verified board/link and calibrated tool revision; retain raw per-step output rather than translating it into a generic script.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: LTSSM margin scope, Intel guide authority and 60 attended/720 machine minutes remain; no sweep value is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Approve the slot/link matrix and guide, prove calibration and recovery, collect baseline, execute the lab-controlled sweep, stop on instability, restore state and compare every result to the guide.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact source authority, physical topology, calibration, per-point evidence, safe boundaries and restoration while retaining the Intel lab method.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Generic OS PCIe status, AER logs or software link queries cannot replace electrical/protocol margining performed by the approved SSV tool and fixtures.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Margin operations can destabilize links or leave settings changed, and results are invalid if probes or manual revisions do not match the platform.

project_override_considerations: An alternative vendor or board-level margin tool requires a documented equivalence matrix for the same slots, LTSSM states, sweep dimensions and limits. Read-only link-health evidence alone is reduced coverage.
expected_evidence: Board/slot/device/root-port/BDF/gen/width identity and approved Intel guide revision
Tool, fixture, probe and instrument versions, calibration and connection/setup photos
Per-margin-point command/configuration, raw tool/probe output, link state, AER/DPC and timestamp evidence
All stop/instability events and operator actions
Fixture removal, restored settings/link/device health, guide comparison and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently delegate the LTSSM margin method and oracle to the Intel validation guide. The missing revision and values are required external artifacts, not contradictory source operations.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The guide, toolchain, calibration, topology and limits are identifiable vendor/lab inputs. They prevent execution now but the intended physical margin test remains clear.

review_improvement: Keeps the correct manual/lab boundary and transforms an unspecified guide reference into an auditable authority, topology, calibration, per-step safety and restoration contract without fabricating margin values.
independent_technical_reasoning: Margining intentionally approaches a link's operating boundary, so the same numeric sweep can be safe and meaningful on one topology but invalid or disruptive on another. Manual revision, probe calibration and physical port identity therefore define the test itself, while software evidence only corroborates the link response.
